propositions: The primary completion-verify agent step is dispatched with no tool_step_limit set, so RunRequest lacks a forced-landing boundary and budget exhaustion kills the run instead of landing a verdict.

Runaway tool-call loops are detected during the run (distinct_ratio_window ≤ 0.50 over a 24-call window) but the detector has no actuator wired to it, leaving the old adjacent-only metric (max_consecutive_repeat) blind to k-cycles with k≥2.

When the agent loops, pydantic-ai raises UsageLimitExceeded → LLMRunnerError; CompletionAgentStep.run catches only UnretryableOutputError, so the runaway fails to reach bounded recovery and raises a bare LLMError with no verdict and no diagnostic.

The flat step budget (240 requests, 480 tool calls) bounds failures but is currently never reached by an actuator—only by exhaustion—leaving --force-close as the only documented exit from a verdict-less state.

Four independent measured occurrences (e369, aec1, 895c, and the 8b97 close itself) confirm loops burn 40–70% of budget on repeated identical tool calls while scaling ranges from single-ticket to 59-descendant epic, proving the defect is structural not capacity-driven.
